concepts.name: kudos
concepts.definition: The unit of recognition a giver gives a recipient. The word is the same in the singular and the plural: 1 kudos, 3 kudos. Not a point, credit or currency, and not a taco: :taco: is only the default kudos emoji.

rejected.because: Michael chose the safe set of rejected names in grilling #8

concepts.name: member
concepts.definition: An active human in a workspace where Kudos is installed, guests included. Only members give and receive kudos; bots, deactivated people and people from another workspace are not members.

concepts.name: giver
concepts.definition: The member who gives kudos, by writing a kudos message or by chiming in on one, and spends their own daily allowance, then weekly reserve, on it.

concepts.name: recipient
concepts.definition: A member mentioned in a kudos message who receives its kudos. Every recipient receives one kudos for each kudos emoji in the message.

concepts.name: daily allowance
concepts.definition: How many kudos a giver can still give today from the workspace's base, minus what they have given today, and never below zero. It starts fresh at midnight in the giver's time zone, and nothing carries over. Bonus capacity from perks is the weekly reserve, spent only after the daily allowance is used up.

concepts.name: kudos emoji
concepts.definition: An emoji that gives kudos for a giver: the workspace's emoji, :taco: unless changed, plus any the giver has unlocked. Each occurrence in a kudos message is one kudos for every recipient.

concepts.name: kudos message
concepts.definition: A message by a member with at least one kudos emoji and at least one mention. Only the message's own text counts, not code, quotes, strikethrough or attachments. It costs the giver one kudos per recipient per kudos emoji.

concepts.name: attempt
concepts.definition: The evaluation of one kudos message against the rules and the giver's daily allowance. It ends in an outcome, and a retry evaluates it again. A message has at most one attempt and gives kudos at most once.

concepts.name: outcome
concepts.definition: How an attempt ended: Given (its recipients received kudos), Over allowance (it cost more than the daily allowance and weekly reserve left, so nothing was given) or Invalid (no mention could receive kudos).

concepts.name: award
concepts.definition: The kudos one giver gave one recipient through one kudos message or one chime-in. An award is permanent: neither editing nor deleting the message, nor removing a reaction, changes it (ADR-0001). Not a grant or gift.

rejected.because: Michael chose the safe set of rejected names in grilling #8

concepts.name: retry
concepts.definition: An edit to a message that has not given kudos which changes its mentions or kudos emoji, so it is evaluated again as if it were new. A retry that gives kudos spends the daily allowance of the day of the edit, then the weekly reserve; removing every kudos emoji instead withdraws the attempt.

concepts.name: skipped mention
concepts.definition: A mention in a kudos message that cannot receive kudos: the giver, a bot, a group or broadcast, or someone who is not a member. The other recipients still receive.

concepts.name: xp
concepts.definition: Experience a member earns from Given awards: 10 for each kudos given and 5 for each kudos received, plus bonus XP from perks, boosters and group auras the member chose, and from chime-in thresholds on kudos they received. XP decides the member's level and never goes down (ADR-0002). It is not kudos and not coins.

concepts.name: level
concepts.definition: A member's rank in progression, from 1 upward with no cap, reached through XP: level 2 at 20 XP, level 3 at 100 XP, and from level L the next level needs 100 × (L − 1) more. Every level up from level 2 gives one skill point.

concepts.name: skill point
concepts.definition: What a level up gives, spent on perks. Unspent skill points never expire, and a spent one is never refunded (ADR-0002). It is not kudos and not a coin.

concepts.name: perk
concepts.definition: Something a member owns for good from the perk list. An effect perk's first step costs skill points and its upgrade costs skill points and coins; an expression perk is bought with coins. Some need a minimum level. An active perk works only for a limited time after the member switches it on.

concepts.name: group aura
concepts.definition: The effect of a group perk: one member buys it, and every member who opted in and has the same primary group as its owner benefits. It follows its owner when they change primary group. Only the strongest aura of each kind counts, however many members own it.

concepts.name: booster
concepts.definition: A temporary effect that raises a member's bonus XP or chance of drops for a set time: an XP booster, a Discovery Lantern or a Crowd booster. Only one of each kind is active at a time.

concepts.name: weekly reserve
concepts.definition: Bonus kudos from perks for one week, spent only after the daily allowance is used up. It refills on Monday at midnight in the giver's time zone, and nothing carries over.

concepts.name: coin
concepts.definition: The currency a member earns from thoughtful giving and from being thanked by many different people, and spends in the store and on perk upgrades (ADR-0003). Coins never turn into kudos, and kudos never turn into coins.

concepts.name: store
concepts.definition: Where members spend coins on items they see before buying: cosmetics, XP boosters, the Discovery Lantern and streak freezes. Nothing in it is a random draw.

concepts.name: cosmetic
concepts.definition: An unlock that changes how a member's kudos look, never what they are worth: a quip, a card, a title or a kudos emoji. Every cosmetic has a rarity.

concepts.name: quip
concepts.definition: An unlocked flavour line the app posts under a kudos message when its giver uses one, so everyone in the channel can see it.

concepts.name: card
concepts.definition: An unlocked image the app shows with a quip, in a celebration or in the collection. A card is not a sticker: a sticker is a person in the sticker book.

concepts.name: title
concepts.definition: An unlocked name a member can show next to their own, such as Bridge Builder.

concepts.name: loadout
concepts.definition: The cosmetics a member has chosen to show: a title, a card, quips and kudos emoji.

concepts.name: collection
concepts.definition: Every cosmetic a member has unlocked, shown privately in App Home.

concepts.name: rarity
concepts.definition: How rare a cosmetic is: common, uncommon, rare, epic or legendary, each with its World of Warcraft colour. Rarity says nothing about the recognition behind it.

concepts.name: drop
concepts.definition: A cosmetic a member finds by chance through a thoughtful kudos they gave. The chance rises after every miss and starts over after a find, and the same cosmetic never drops twice.

concepts.name: unlock
concepts.definition: Something a member gains for good through progression: a cosmetic or a perk (ADR-0002).

concepts.name: achievement
concepts.definition: One tier of a ladder, earned once by doing something, such as thanking ten different people. It gives an exclusive cosmetic, never XP, skill points or coins, and it is never taken back.

rejected.because: use achievement or tier, never badge

concepts.name: ladder
concepts.definition: A series of four achievements for the same kind of action, each harder than the one before.

concepts.name: tier
concepts.definition: An achievement's place on its ladder: bronze, silver, gold or diamond. A tier is not a rarity.

concepts.name: streak
concepts.definition: A run of a member's workdays on which they gave at least one kudos. Days off and paused days neither add to it nor break it.

concepts.name: workday
concepts.definition: A day of the week a member works, Monday to Friday unless they change it. Only workdays count for streaks.

concepts.name: pause
concepts.definition: A future date a member marks as away, such as a holiday. It never breaks a streak and costs nothing.

concepts.name: freeze
concepts.definition: A store item that covers one missed workday so a streak survives, at most two missed workdays in a row. It adds no day to the streak.

concepts.name: thoughtful kudos
concepts.definition: A kudos message that says why its recipients earned it: for now, at least five words besides the mentions and kudos emoji. Only thoughtful kudos trigger bonus XP, perk effects, drops and coins, and spend the weekly reserve; every Given award still earns base XP.

concepts.name: chime-in
concepts.definition: A member's click on the app's kudos reaction under a given kudos message within a day of it, once per member and message; the message's giver and recipients cannot chime in. It gives each recipient one more kudos from the clicker's daily allowance, then weekly reserve, is thoughtful when the message was, and counts toward the message's chime-in thresholds.

rejected.because: the owner's later-feature name became the chime-in

concepts.name: chime-in threshold
concepts.definition: A number of chime-ins on one kudos message (3, 5, 10, 20, 50 or 100). Reaching one gives everyone who chimed in, and the giver, a stronger Crowd booster, and gives the recipients bonus XP.

concepts.name: sticker book
concepts.definition: A member's private album of the people they have thanked and the people who have thanked them, one sticker each, with an album for every group to complete: an album is complete once the member has thanked or been thanked by every other current member of the group, and it stays complete.

concepts.name: sticker
concepts.definition: A person in a member's sticker book. A sticker is not a cosmetic image, which is a card.

concepts.name: announcement channel
concepts.definition: A public channel a workspace admin picks for level-up and achievement notices, instead of the thread under the kudos message.

concepts.name: xp booster
concepts.definition: A store item that, once switched on, adds a quarter to the base XP of the kudos a member gives for seven days. It never boosts received XP, and it adds to perk bonuses without compounding.

concepts.name: discovery lantern
concepts.definition: A store item that, once switched on, raises a member's chance of drops by a quarter for seven days. It never gives extra draws.

concepts.name: crowd booster
concepts.definition: A booster for 24 hours that a chime-in threshold gives everyone who chimed in on a kudos message and its giver, stronger at each higher threshold. Only the strongest Crowd booster a member holds counts.

concepts.name: group
concepts.definition: A Slack user group that counts for Kudos: every enabled custom user group unless a workspace admin picked an allowlist, never Slack's automatic admin and owner groups. A member can be in several groups. A group mention in a kudos message is still a skipped mention.

concepts.name: primary group
concepts.definition: The one group a member's kudos count for on the leaderboard, and whose group auras they can receive. A member in one group has it automatically; a member in several picks one in the welcome message or App Home, and until then it is the smallest. The primary group is stored with each award when it is given, so history never moves.

concepts.name: leaderboard
concepts.definition: A positive ranking of kudos given in a period (this week, this month or all time, by the giver's allowance day): groups by kudos given per member, then participation; and members inside their primary group or across the workspace, showing the top 3 and the member with the 3 people above and below. It never ranks kudos received or XP, and a member can leave the individual boards.

concepts.name: participation
concepts.definition: The share of a group's members who gave at least one kudos in a period. It breaks ties between groups on the leaderboard.

concepts.name: welcome message
concepts.definition: The one DM the app sends a member the first time they give or receive a Given award: how Kudos works, and, once groups exist, the pick of their primary group.

concepts.name: profile card
concepts.definition: What any member sees of another member: name, equipped title and card, primary group, and level and achievement tiers unless hidden. Never coins, perks, streaks, XP or kudos received.

concepts.name: sandbox
concepts.definition: The Slack workspace and its own Convex deployment where a new Kudos app is installed and proven before the real install. It runs a separate Slack app from the same manifest, with its own bot token and signing secret.

concepts.name: directory
concepts.definition: The app's record of a workspace's people: whether each is a member, a bot or not a member, and their time zone. Slack keeps it fresh, eligibility and the allowance day are read from it when a kudos message is evaluated, and a person it doesn't know makes the message wait.

concepts.name: indicator
concepts.definition: The one reaction the app shows on a kudos message for its outcome: the first kudos emoji the giver used for Given, an hourglass for Over allowance, a red X for Invalid, and none otherwise. It is desired state, so every delivery leaves the message showing the latest one.

concepts.name: domain event
concepts.definition: A fact a module publishes when something happened in the domain, such as kudosGiven, so that later modules react to it without the publisher knowing them. It is published in the transaction that made it true, and its shape only grows by adding fields.

concepts.name: hook
concepts.definition: A named point where a later module contributes to a decision another module makes without that module knowing it, such as the parse hooks of the kudos parser and, with the weekly reserve, the perks hook. Not the agent-host hooks that deliver Coherence.

concepts.name: parse hook
concepts.definition: A hook into the kudos parser: it names extra kudos emoji for a giver, or adds annotations about a message while its text is in memory. The workspace emoji hook names the workspace's kudos emoji; the thoughtful kudos hook adds the gate decision.

concepts.name: annotation
concepts.definition: A fact about a kudos message that a parse hook adds while the text is in memory, such as whether it says why, carried on kudosGiven in place of the text, which is never stored.

concepts.name: revision
concepts.definition: One version of a chat message as the app saw it: the post, then each edit. Revisions are ordered (in Slack, by the edit's time, else the message's own), and a revision at or below the newest the app has seen for that message is ignored, so an original that arrives after its edit or a late older edit changes nothing (R21). A kudos message keeps only its newest revision, never its text.

concepts.name: app home
concepts.definition: A member's private page of Kudos in Slack, the app's Home tab. It shows how to give kudos, the daily allowance left today and when it refills, and the kudos the member gave and received this week and in total; later specs add their sections.

concepts.name: HedgeHug
concepts.definition: The product's name as members see it: the Slack app, the bot, the slash command and the website. Code, classes and docs keep calling the product Kudos. Hug is flavour only, never the unit: the unit stays kudos.

concepts.name: website
concepts.definition: The signed-in browser surface where a member sees and manages their Kudos. It sits beside App Home and never replaces it.

concepts.name: effects record
concepts.definition: What progression writes once for one side of one award, the giver's or the recipient's: the base XP with the gate decision and the catalogue version in force, and in later stopping points the bonus XP, coins and drops. Effects records are insert-only and never recomputed (ADR-0004); a member's XP, level and skill points are derived from them.

concepts.name: gate decision
concepts.definition: Whether a kudos message is thoughtful kudos, decided once per revision by the thoughtful kudos parse hook from the text in memory and stored as an annotation: the rule version, thoughtful or not, and the word count. A recheck reuses it, a retry decides again, and every effects record copies the version and the verdict (P12).

concepts.name: levelReached
concepts.definition: The domain event progression publishes when a kudosGiven brings a member to a higher level: one per member and event, naming the highest level reached and the skill points it gave, with the kudos message that caused it (P6). Level-up DMs and public notices react to it.
